transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-12
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jules Nguyen (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Horizon - Head of ML), Tom Alvarez (Horizon - Platform), Priya Singh (Horizon - PM)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda: recap last week's tuning, share the updated benchmark spreadsheet, run through outstanding asks (security + traffic), and align on next steps for the exec closeout. Maya you good to kick us off with any quick context?

[00:15] Maya: Yeah, thanks Samir. Uh, overall pilot going well, customers -- sorry, our internal stakeholders saw quality improvements on the product-recommendation flow. The main things for us are 1) p95 latency under peak (we need < 450ms), 2) cost at scale, and 3) the compliance checklist for production. We also want a final ROI so we can take to the execs.

[01:05] Jules: Great. Quick summary from the SE side: after enabling prefix KV-cache + conservative batching we saw token-per-request cpu drop and p50 improved ~18%, p95 improved about 12% on hosted. I shared the "benchmarks.xlsx" in the chat (link: https://redwood-internal/sandbox/pilot/benchmarks.xlsx) with raw runs. There's some noise at peak QPS because of concurrency limits on the current hosted pool.

[02:15] Tom: I pulled our traffic profile into the sheet, you can see the QPS spikes around 9am and 6pm PST, average seq length is 320 tokens but 95th is around 1.2k. That's where we see the latency step-up.

[03:02] Jules: Right, the 1.2k sequences trigger longer KV eviction and memory pressure, so the runtime switches to a different kernel path causing a latency tail. For dedicated we can pin a quantized variant and increase KV cache to reduce the tail. Early numbers show p99 could go from 1.8s->0.9s with the dedicated config and larger cache.

[04:20] Priya: Just to clarify: our success criteria from product is end-user 95th percentile under 450ms and model accuracy lift of at least +4% over baseline recommendation. Does that map to what you see in the data?

[04:55] Jules: Accuracy is within the target, we've measured ~4.5% uplift on the A/B slices in week 3. Latency is near target on typical traffic but fails with the long-tail sequences during peak.

[06:10] Maya: So it sounds like dedicated is the safer path for the exec ask. But we also need to know the cost delta and nitty-gritty on SLA and audit logs.

[06:35] Samir: Yep that's the tradeoff. For reference we've prepared a hosted vs dedicated TCO model. High-level: hosted incremental cost per 1M tokens is lower initially but dedicated gives predictable p95 and better tail behavior when you size for peak. I'll send the ROI sheet after this meeting.

[07:30] Tom: On the compliance side, we're still waiting for the SOC2 attestation and the exact KMS integration docs. Maya flagged that for legal.

[08:05] Samir: Understood. We'll share the SOC2 letter and KMS/HSM integration guide. Jules, can you drop the security packet in the drive link? (Jules: yes)

[08:30] Jules: Dropped link in chat: https://drive.redwood/security/horizon-pilot. Docs include SOC2 summary, SSO/SAML setup notes, and audit log retention options. Note that the private deployment option supports customer-managed KMS in our VPC flow.

[09:10] Priya: Great. Back to benchmarks — can you walk us through the dedicated config numbers again?

[09:30] Jules: Sure. Two runs we did last night under dedicated sizing: Config A (4x A100-like GPUs, fp16, 16k cache) gave p50=120ms, p95=380ms, p99=920ms average at 600 qps steady. Config B (2x + aggressive quantization int8, 8k cache) gave p50=95ms, p95=460ms, p99=1.6s. Config B is cheaper but p95 slightly above your 450ms threshold, and p99 is unstable. So if p95 is hard requirement go with Config A.

[11:05] Maya: That matches the pattern we saw. What's the cost delta between A and B for monthly committed usage?

[11:20] Samir: Rough numbers: Config A committed (reserved) estimated $65k/month for Horizon's projected 1B tokens/mo profile; Config B about $42k/month. Hosted at the observed traffic hits about $48k/mo but with higher variance and potential throttling at peak. I'll put detailed numbers in the ROI sheet.

[12:00] Tom: Are those committed prices including support and SLOs?

[12:15] Samir: Yes, committed includes standard enterprise SLA and 24/7 on-call, plus a premium for the larger cache reservation. Add-ons like longer observability retention cost extra.

[13:02] Priya: On security, if we go committed dedicated in our VPC, do we still get the same logging hooks? Our compliance team requires audit trails per request for at least 180 days.

[13:30] Jules: Yes, dedicated in VPC supports per-request audit logs and we can integrate with your SIEM; retention is configurable, 180 days is supported as an add-on. There are costs and storage sizing to be agreed.

[14:10] Maya: Okay. One thing we noticed: occasionally the model regression test flagged a small hallucination increase after quantization on some SKU descriptions. How are we tracking quality regressions?

[14:45] Jules: Good catch. We run regression evals on our eval harness each change. For the int8 runs we saw a 0.7% drop on the hallucination metric for a specific SKU slice; we can re-tune quantization knobs (per-layer) or fall back to fp16 for those sequences. We recommend a targeted per-route policy: quantize non-critical routes, keep fp16 for catalog-sensitive prompts.

[16:00] Maya: That's actionable — we need a list of recommended route policies and a plan for auto-fallback when regressions appear.

[16:20] Samir: We'll include recommended policies in the handoff doc and set up an alert tied to the eval suite so if regression >0.5% an automatic canary rollback triggers. Action item for Jules to configure that.

[17:05] Tom: Quick question on model pinning and rollouts — we want to be able to roll back within 10 minutes if something breaks. How fast are rollouts in Dedicated?

[17:25] Jules: Rollouts are ~1-3 minutes for route-level changes, full model swap across the fleet can be 5-15 minutes depending on warm cache and KV rehydration. We can do canary first to minimize impact.

[18:10] Priya: Sounds fine. For the exec packet we need three things: 1) final ROI/TCO, 2) security/compliance artifacts, 3) clear success criteria and recommended config. Can Redwood commit to delivering those by 2026-02-19?

[18:40] Samir: Yes, can commit. Jules will produce the final benchmark run logs, I'll prepare the ROI and exec summary, and we'll bundle the security docs.

[19:05] Maya: On the timeline - assuming we agree to dedicated after the closeout, when could we expect a production cutover? We have a target of end of Q2 2026.

[19:30] Samir: If decision by late Feb, provisioning and on-prem-like VPC setup typically takes 4-6 weeks, plus a 2-week ramp for validation. So end of Q2 is feasible. We'll put a timeline in the exec packet.

[20:20] Priya: Are we tracking blockers? From our side: legal signoff and budget approval. From Redwood side: final security #s and committed pricing. Anything else?

[20:40] Jules: Technical blockers: need Tom's traffic profile and permission to run the dedicated benchmark on a full load representative of peak traffic.

[21:05] Tom: I'll drop the profile and give access.

[21:30] Samir: Recap of decisions and next steps: 1) Redwood to deliver ROI + detailed hosted vs dedicated comparison by 2026-02-19; 2) SE to run two dedicated benchmarks (Config A & B) and share raw logs by 2026-02-18; 3) Security packet (SOC2, KMS guide, audit log options) delivered today in drive; 4) Horizon to confirm success criteria and exec attendees by 2026-02-17.

[22:15] Maya: Sounds good. Any other questions?

[22:25] Priya: One small ask — can you include cost sensitivity (what if tokens increase 25%/50%) in the ROI? Helps our finance team model scenarios.

[22:40] Samir: Yes, we'll include sensitivity scenarios.

[23:00] Jules: Also note — we found a small bug in the metrics exporter on the hosted pool (some p99 samples were mis-labeled). I've filed an internal ticket and won't affect the main numbers but I'll flag any changes in the benchmark sheet.

[23:45] Tom: Ok thanks.

[24:00] Samir: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and set up the exec closeout meeting.

[24:15] Meeting ended.

Notes on transcription quality: intermittent mislabels, some technical terms transcribed imperfectly (e.g., KV cache as "K-V cash" in a few lines), occasional run-on sentences.

References shared in chat: ROI sheet (https://redwood-internal/sandbox/pilot/roi_horizon.xlsx), Benchmarks (https://redwood-internal/sandbox/pilot/benchmarks.xlsx), Security packet (https://drive.redwood/security/horizon-pilot)
